# Manual notification plugin workflows

**Bump version** and **Build** are independent manual workflows. Neither starts the
other. There are no tag-triggered builds or automatic branch/PR builds.

Run **Bump version** on a branch with the required `patch`, `minor`, or `major`
choice (default `patch`). It validates the selected immutable source and remote
branch, makes one source-only direct-child commit with the Actions bot identity
and Copilot App trailer, and pushes only that exact branch update. It never tags,
builds, releases, or dispatches another workflow. Concurrent branch movement,
including rewind/deletion/same-result advertisement races, stops the update.
The committed executable pre-push guard is mandatory; do not bypass it.

Run **Build** separately using Actions' built-in branch/tag selector. It has no
custom inputs and no default-branch restriction. Every checkout uses the event's
immutable `github.sha`, not a subsequently moving branch name. The version is
derived from source; publication is serialized across all refs without
cancellation (GitHub concurrency does not promise FIFO ordering).

## Source authority

The original Bump header at `5f0e126b303dafc2f4f71abf5a68eed7792bee10`
explicitly coordinates both `MARKETING_VERSION` and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`.
Its implementation incorrectly updated only the selected marketing key.
At intake `c23581e26397058c627e8d0e065c5c955d38a5f7`, the three project-level
Development/Deployment/Default marketing values were already **2.6.1** while
the three current values and copied English localization were **2.6.0**.
This migration aligns only those stale source tokens to **2.6.1**; it does not
increment the existing authority.

`Info.plist` requires `CFBundleShortVersionString` and retains its
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` reference. Its absent `CFBundleVersion` stays
absent. Bump updates only literal version tokens in the Xcode project, source
plist where applicable, and `English.lproj/InfoPlist.strings`. Encoding, BOM,
individual newline separators, modes, references and unrelated bytes are
preserved. Duplicate, missing, unresolved, cyclic or drifting metadata fails
before writes. Destination localization, tracked plugin binaries, Windows
projects, 4D data/counters, manifests and other resources are not version sources.

## Native and publication policy

The original workflow is actually macOS-only despite its Windows-build comments.
Build keeps `Default`, `arm64 x86_64`, `ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO`, the **11.0** deployment
override, frameworks, resources, prebuilt Windows64 payload and original
`Notification Center.4dbase/Plugins/Notification Center.bundle` artifact.
The project has no gitlinks or dependency build recipes.

Unlike the other configurations, Default does not set `CONFIGURATION_BUILD_DIR`;
its inherited configuration suffix could otherwise leave the original packaged
bundle stale. Build explicitly directs its fresh output to that original artifact
directory, not to a sibling `Default` bundle. Only proven generated leaves and
product intermediate roots are cleaned, after symlink/reparse prevalidation.
Unrelated bundle resources and tracked prebuilts are retained. The legacy native
sign/notary shell phase is unchanged and runs only for **Deployment**, not Default.
`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` suppresses Xcode's built-in signing; explicit workflow
signing still follows the fresh build.

Unsigned validation is separate from signed validation. Exact architecture tokens,
source-derived XML/binary plist and compiled/text localization, exact copied
resources, nonempty regular nonsymlink packaged leaves, strict code-signature
verification, successful notarization with JSON `Accepted`, and DMG stapling are
required. Original runtime-architecture scope is unchanged. ZIP and DMG names
remain `Notification Center-X.Y.Z.zip` and `.dmg`; GitHub converts spaces in their
remote asset names to dots. Release body remains empty, without generated notes.

Before native work and after signing/notarization/stapling, explicit `GH_TOKEN`
and the exact canonical repository `miyako/4d-plugin-user-notification` are
required. Every release page (including drafts) is read until an empty page;
exact API refs and the independent remote tag advertisement must be absent.
Initial checkout validation requires clean source. Final validation permits only
exact generated worktree outputs, assets, controlled product intermediates and
`build/XCBuildData/build.db`, its `-wal`/`-shm` companions, or lowercase 32-hex
`.xcbuilddata` descendants. HEAD, complete index, raw nongenerated bytes, hidden
index flags and unexpected untracked/ignored files remain protected. Generated
bytes are retained, never reset to make the checkout appear clean.

Publication separately creates a tag at the selected SHA, verifies its exact
API/remote identity, creates a new public release with a new positive ID, then
uploads the exact two assets to that ID. It never reuses or updates releases,
clobbers assets, deletes, rolls back, or retries mutations.

## Manual recovery

On failure, inspect the reported retained state: the branch commit, tag, release
ID and confirmed or uncertain uploads may already exist. A failed response can
hide a successful server mutation. **Do not rerun blindly**: inspect exact remote
refs and draft/public releases first. Resolve partial publication manually with
the repository owner, or choose a new source version through the independent
Bump workflow. Automation intentionally performs no cleanup or rollback.

## Offline validation

Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and
`actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml`. Tests use real disposable Git repositories
and bare remotes, fake `gh`, and closed-PATH native/credential stubs. They do not
invoke real native builds, signing, notarization or 4D, and do not read secrets.
These doubles establish protocol and orchestration behavior, not hosted
toolchain/service availability. Immutable prior-art blob provenance is recorded
in `tests/reference-pins.json`.
